title: Sourdough country loaf
equipment: banneton or bowl with tea towel

ingredients.name: active sourdough starter (100 % hydration)
ingredients.original: 100 g active sourdough starter (100 % hydration), fed 4–8 hours before

steps.text: Mix the flours with 325 ml of the water until no dry flour remains. Cover and rest.
Add the starter and squeeze it in, then add the salt with the remaining water and mix until fully absorbed.
Bulk ferment at about 24 °C, giving the dough a set of stretch and folds every 30 minutes for the first 2 hours.
steps.critical: Judge by the dough, not the clock: it should rise by about half, feel airy and jiggle, with bubbles on the sides.

steps.text: Turn out, pre-shape into a loose round and let it rest uncovered.
Shape into a tight round or oval and put it seam side up in a basket dusted with rice flour.
Heat the Dutch oven in the oven.
Turn the cold dough onto parchment, score it and bake in the covered pot for 20 minutes, then uncover and bake at 230 °C for 25 minutes until deep brown.
Cool on a rack before slicing.

notes.techniques: An overnight cold retard develops sour flavour and makes the cold dough easy to score.
notes.chemistry: Wild yeasts produce gas while lactic and acetic acid bacteria add sourness; steam trapped in the lidded pot keeps the crust soft long enough for full oven spring. The loaf is done at about 96 °C inside.
notes.variations: A wheat loaf with a free-form open crumb and a blistered crust, unlike the dense, tin-baked rye.

ingredients.name: caraway or fennel seeds
ingredients.original: 1 tsp caraway or fennel seeds, lightly crushed (optional)

steps.text: Stir the starter into the water, then mix in the flours, salt, syrup and seeds to a thick, sticky paste. Do not knead.
Scrape into the oiled tin and smooth the top with a wet spatula.
Cover and leave until risen by about a third and small cracks appear on the surface.
Bake at 230 °C for 15 minutes, then lower to 200 °C and bake until the inside reaches about 98 °C.
Turn out, cool, wrap in a towel and leave before slicing.
steps.critical: Cut too early and the crumb is gummy; rye needs many hours to set.

notes.techniques: Rye dough is mixed, not kneaded, and baked in a tin because it cannot hold its shape.
notes.chemistry: Rye has little usable gluten; its structure comes from pentosans that absorb lots of water, and the acidity of the sourdough stops rye enzymes from breaking down the starch into a gummy crumb.
notes.spiceProfile: Earthy rye, malty sweetness from the syrup and caraway or fennel.
notes.variations: A dense, moist, mildly sweet tin loaf that keeps for a week, very different from an open-crumbed wheat country loaf.
